newsitem.title: ITALY: World's largest passenger ship launched in Italy.
newsitem.headline: World's largest passenger ship launched in Italy.

text.p: The world's largest cruise ship passenger, the Grand Princess, was launched on Thursday at state shipbuilder Fincantieri's Monfalcone shipyard in northeast Italy.

Alison Ratcliffe, wife of the P&O Group's Princess Cruises Ltd Chairman Peter Ratcliffe, broke a bottle of champagne over the ship's bow as the gleaming white, 109,000 gross ton monster towered above the dry dock.
The vessel on Friday will be floated to a nearby outfitting pier for interior completion before handover in spring 1998 when it will become the flagship of the Princess Cruises fleet.
The $400 million, 285 metre long (935 feet) Grand Princess will have 1,296 cabins with a maximum capacity of 3,300 passengers and a crew of 1,100.
Its maiden voyage, from Southampton to Istanbul, is scheduled for May next year.
The vessel is the fifth Fincantieri has built for P&0 at Monfalcone after the 70,000 ton sister ships Crown Princess and Regal Princess and the 77,000 ton Sun and Dawn Princess.
Fincantieri Chairman Corrado Antonini noted that the Italian yard will also be building for P&O Princess Cruises two new 77,000 ton ships, the Sea Princess and Ocean Princess.
Peter Ratcliffe said the Grand Princess had been built with the most advanced security systems.
"This is the first vessel to be built at Monfalcone using a new mobile, completely robotised workshop designed and built by Fincantieri under the European Eureka project," he said.
The Grand Princess will feature a virtual reality centre, five pools, a glass-walled night club suspended 150 feet above the stern, as well as a nine-hole putting green and computerised golf centre.
The world's previous largest cruise liner, the 101,000 ton Carnival Destiny, also built by Fincantieri at Monfalcone, was delivered to the U.S. Carnival Corp's Carnival Cruise Lines last October.

The launch of the Grand Princess confirms Fincantieri's leading role among the few world's shipyards capable of building large cruise vessels, with a market share of over 40 percent in terms of gross tonnage.

From the mid-1980s, the Trieste-headquartered company has gained orders on the world market for 21 cruise ships -- 10 of which have already been handed over -- for an overall value of over 11 trillion lire ($6.6 billion).
Fincantieri's current orderbook for the remaining 11 vessels to be handed over totals over 6.5 trillion lire.
In 1996, the group posted a 50.3 billion lire profit against 25.2 billion the previous year with a production value up six percent to 3.52 billion lire. $=1,662 lire
